summary: Burst of 5xxs from upstream CUDA stall during concurrent multipart embeddings upload
description: Customer LexiSearch reported a sudden increase in 5xx responses when uploading large embedding batches using multipart/form-data to the /v1/embeddings/bulk endpoint. Errors correlated with GPU stalls and NVMe IO spikes on several serving hosts. This ticket captures the investigation, mitigation, and post-incident actions.
impact: From ~0.2% 5xx baseline to ~8% for the customer's tenant over a 22-minute window. Multiple long-lived multipart upload connections stalled and retried, causing downstream rate amplification and degraded latency for other tenants in the same availability zone. A single enterprise customer experienced failed batch uploads, blocking ingestion pipelines.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the embeddings bulk endpoint with multipart upload (500+ files, mixed small/large payloads). 2) Send concurrent clients (10-20 parallel connections) from a single tenant in us-west-2. 3) Observe elevated 5xx rate within ~5-10 minutes and timeouts on large chunks. 4) Reproduce is rate-dependent and requires sustained concurrent multipart streams.
observed_logs:
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] runtime-0a3b: ERROR serving: request failed: upstream: runtime SIGTIMEOUT after 120s
[2026-03-10T14:12:05Z] nvme-io-monitor: WARN io-queue-depth=512 -> latency_ms p50=18 p99=420
[2026-03-10T14:13:11Z] gpu-0b7: ERROR CUDA driver stall detected: kernel_timeout=3000ms, resetting context
[2026-03-10T14:13:12Z] api-gw: 502 returned to client tenant=lexisearch route=/v1/embeddings/bulk count=73
[2026-03-10T14:14:01Z] runtime: worker-exit pid=2124 status=137 oom_killer=false
investigation_notes: Initial telemetry showed a tight coupling between multipart read buffer bursts and NVMe io-queue spikes. Serving runtime logs included repeated 'CUDA driver stall' warnings preceding worker exits. Heap and stack traces pointed at the embedding sharder code path where large payload assembly occurs. Autoscaler did not immediately add capacity due to prewarm-policy misalignment for long-lived streaming uploads. Grafana dashboards: dashboards/embeddings/tenant-lexisearch (link in slack). Slack thread: #support 2026-03-10T14:20 (https://slack.redwood/support/T08P0...). Hypothesis: concurrent multipart uploads cause backpressure into the runtime's temp staging on NVMe which then leads to higher kernel latency; GPUs queue long-running kernels and driver detects stall leading to context reset and runtime worker restarts, amplifying 5xx. Verified by correlating nvme queue depth spikes with GPU stall timestamps.
mitigation: 1) Temporarily add a tenant-level rate limit for multipart/bulk embedding uploads for LexiSearch to 5 concurrent streams. 2) Adjust API gateway to prefer streaming chunked approach (switch off full-file buffer path) for the tenant. 3) Shift active requests from affected hosts by altering routing weight for the customer's route to alternate AZ. These steps reduced immediate 5xx volume within 8 minutes.
resolution_notes: Root cause was identified as a staging buffer pressure bug in the embedding multipart assembler that allowed NVMe IO bursts to queue excessively under concurrent uploads; this caused long GPU kernel queues and eventual CUDA driver stall/reset. Fix deployed: PR https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/8429 which adds backpressure at assembler read, streams large parts instead of full buffering, and caps NVMe io-queue per tenant. Patch rolled out to us-west on 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC. Post-deploy: 5xx for LexiSearch returned to baseline (~0.3%) and no further CUDA stalls observed for same workload in a 48-hour verification window.
follow_up_actions:
- Monitor nvme queue depth and gpu stall metrics and create an alert threshold (nvme_p99 > 300ms AND gpu_stall_count > 1 in 5m)
- Add a runbook for multipart bulk ingestion (RB-embed-02) describing safe concurrency limits and recommended chunking
- Evaluate autoscaler prewarm policy for long-lived uploads to ensure capacity scales sooner for streaming workloads
- Add tenant-level default backpressure settings to embeddings-service
